newsitem.title: USA: DSM unit sues Sepracor and Tanabe over patent.
newsitem.headline: DSM unit sues Sepracor and Tanabe over patent.

text.p: The licensing subsidiary of the Dutch chemicals group DSM NV is suing Sepracor Inc and Tanabe Seiyaku Co Ltd in a patent dispute.

In papers filed Monday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, the DSM unit Stamicarbon BV challenged the companies' claim to be the first inventors of a process for making a drug used to treat heart and blood pressure disorders.
The unit said that in November the Board of patent Appeals "erroneously" awarded priority of invention to Sepracor and Tanabe for the preparation of esters used to make diltiazem.
Diltiazem is a calcium antagonist used in the treatment of angina pectoris, hypertension, and several other disorders.

Stamicarbon alleged that while the Patent and Trademark Office acknowledged Stamicarbon's Netherlands patent application of May 1988 was the first one filed for the process, the PTO nonetheless denied Stamicarbon the benefit of that priority "for not disclosing the best mode of making and carrying out the invention," court papers say.
Stamicarbon wants the court to order the PTO to reverse the award of priority to Sepracor allowing Stamicarbon to recapture the patent's potential benefits.
A spokeswoman at Sepracor, reached at its Marlborough, Mass. headquarters, said, "This is an appeal of a decision that was rendered favorable toward the Sepracor and Tanabe partnership in November."
Tanabe is a pharmaceutical company based in Osaka, Japan.
